subject: DPA — subprocessors & analytics export: proposed language and sign-off needed
messages:
From: Lisa Hawthorne <lisa.hawthorne@sightlinehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: procurement@sightlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline + question on subprocessors / analytics export

Hi team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and privacy teams reviewed the DPA and attached a redline (Sightline_DPA_redline_v2.pdf). There are two items blocking procurement on our side:

1) Subprocessors: we see an analytics vendor listed in your appendix. Our policy requires a specific security clause and SOC2 evidence for any subprocessor that processes PHI-adjacent metadata. Can you confirm the analytics vendor and provide SOC2 report or confirm they operate under your SCCs?

2) Analytics export: we need clarity on the clause that allows Redwood to export aggregated usage/analytics. We cannot accept any export that contains device identifiers or unhashed user ids. Would Redwood accept a carve-in that limits exports to strictly aggregated, non-identifying metrics (30+ aggregation thresholds), and enforces a 30-day retention for exported data?

Procurement needs a short path to sign the DPA — ideally a proposed redline and a statement from product/security confirming the analytics export constraints. Can you get back by Friday EOD PST?

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Hawthorne
Head of Legal Operations | Sightline Health

Subject: Re: DPA redline + question on subprocessors / analytics export

Thanks for flagging this, team. Quick technical summary from product: 

- Subprocessor: the analytics partner is "FathomMetrics, Inc." (we onboarded them for anonymized usage telemetry). They do have a SOC2 Type II report, but we do not surface their SCCs to customers currently. We can request permission to share their SOC2 summary under NDA if necessary.

- Analytics export: current export pipeline produces two types of artifacts: 
  1) Aggregated dashboards (rollups by tenant, model, and endpoint) — these contain no PII by design.
  2) Diagnostic exports (for debugging) — these can include hashed user ids and partial context.

What we can offer as a standard control today:
- Create a customer-scoped aggregated export only (no hashed/partial contexts) with a 30-day retention and a minimum-grouping threshold (default 50) configurable by contract. Implementation effort: ~2 dev-weeks to add an export filter and a retention TTL knob.

If Sightline needs a 30+ minimum grouping and 30-day retention, product can scope that as a contractual exception tied to a special export role and a controlled request process (customer requests export -> product ops approves -> export generated). That would add ~1 week process work for ops.

If legal/security are comfortable with sharing FathomMetrics SOC2 under NDA, that might accelerate subprocessor signoff.

I can draft proposed language for the DPA carve if you want.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Product Manager, Observability | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: lisa.hawthorne@sightlinehealth.com
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline + question on subprocessors / analytics export

Appreciate the detail. From Security's perspective: 

- Subprocessors: we require either (a) direct SOC2 Type II report for FathomMetrics, or (b) a contractual requirement that FathomMetrics maintain equivalent controls and permit audits under Redwood's agreement. We cannot accept a black-box subprocessor with no evidence when the customer is in healthcare.

- Export concerns: aggregated-only exports are probably acceptable provided:
  * Aggregation threshold is verifiable (we should log that exported artifact meets the threshold),
  * No reversible identifiers are included (hashed ids alone are insufficient without salt control),
  * Exports must be encrypted at rest and in transit, with RBAC showing who requested/exported the data, and
  * Minimum retention of 30 days for downstream logs for audit is ok, but the exported dataset retention must be contractually limited to 30 days and auto-deleted.

Proposed mitigation path (least friction):
1) Share FathomMetrics SOC2 summary under NDA and obtain confirmation of their encryption/KMS posture.
2) We commit to a customer-scoped aggregated export with a 50-band default, configurable to 30 upon legal/security approval, with auto-delete after 30 days and export request logging.
3) Add a subprocessor appendix referencing FathomMetrics and requiring notice + opportunity to object (standard).

Marissa — please propose DPA wording for the above and we can iterate.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Lisa Hawthorne <lisa.hawthorne@sightlinehealth.com>, procurement@sightlinehealth.com

Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline + question on subprocessors / analytics export

Lisa / Procurement — thanks for the patience. We've discussed internally and propose the following path to get you to signature this week: 

1) Subprocessor: Redwood confirms the analytics vendor is FathomMetrics, Inc. We can share FathomMetrics' SOC2 Type II summary under NDA. We will also add an appendix to the DPA naming FathomMetrics and a clause requiring notice + opportunity to object for any new subprocessor.

2) Analytics export: Redwood will provide a customer-scoped aggregated export limited to non-identifying metrics, with the following contractual guarantees:
   - Minimum aggregation threshold: 30 (Sightline requested 30; product scoped to support a 30 threshold via contract).
   - Export retention: exported datasets will be retained for a maximum of 30 days and auto-deleted thereafter.
   - Exports encrypted at rest/in transit; export requests logged with actor identity for audit.

3) Implementation and sign-off: Product estimates ~2 dev-weeks to add export filter + TTL; ops will add a manual approval flow for the first month to ensure process works. Security requires us to share FathomMetrics SOC2 summary under NDA before procurement signs — I can send that under NDA ASAP.

Attached is a proposed DPA redline that incorporates the above (Redwood_proposed_DPA_redline_0608.docx). If that looks ok we can route to DocuSign. If you'd prefer a quick call to walk the redline, I can set aside 30 minutes tomorrow.

Next steps for Sightline: let me know whether you can accept receipt of FathomMetrics SOC2 under NDA and whether the proposed aggregation/retention language is acceptable.

I'll follow up with a DocuSign link if you confirm.

Thanks,
Karthik
